one_bounded_candidate.name: Repeated validation/readback for each surviving source-bound symbol identity
one_bounded_candidate.status: Concrete repeated work found; unmeasured candidate, not a demonstrated bottleneck or required fix.
one_bounded_candidate.trigger: Full snapshot insert_file_data_impl calls insert_on after symbol rows. If symbol_identities is nonempty and an identity passes in-memory validation and SQL-survivor check, the insertion path proceeds through load_on.
one_bounded_candidate.actual_work: First symbol_matches_on SELECT EXISTS at146, then identity INSERT and JSON serialization at149; load_on immediately SELECTs/deserializes that same identity, calls symbol_matches_on again at205, validates joined files/chunks/document_manifest at209, SELECTs/deserializes chunks.source_json at216. Successful path:5SELECT+1INSERT per surviving identity, including the identical symbol match twice. Separate per-file BTreeMap indexes are built for chunks/documents/symbols/boundaries before the loop.
one_bounded_candidate.bounds_and_exclusions: AllSQL uses prepare_cached. Key columns retain PRIMARY KEY/UNIQUE indexes after explicit secondary-index removal (schema files.file_path, chunks.chunk_id, symbols.symbol_id, document_manifest.doc_key/chunk_id, chunk_symbol_identity.chunk_id). This is proportional point-query/JSON work, not demonstrated N-squared table scanning. No query plan or cache-miss count was measured.
one_bounded_candidate.minimal_future_question: Could a private full-rebuild-only verified identity/readback token avoid duplicate checks or serialization without losing SQL survivor authority, provenance validation, first-error ordering, trigger/schema fallback or transaction rollback? This review proposes no patch or control weakening. Need actual attribution before selecting a change.

other_real_global_work_not_a_second_fix_.work: Once per rebuilt snapshot, graph baseline scan_on folds symbols, call_edges, semantic_edges, dispatch_sites and files (5 table queries) into8aggregates using Rust row decoding/hashing. Explicit secondary indexes are recreated once after transaction commit. Both scale with stored rows and are inside full_staging.
other_real_global_work_not_a_second_fix_.exclusion: These are not re-run per file in the inspected call chain. Baseline prevents later full scans and must represent final persisted survivors. Source alone does not show either is redundant or dominates elapsed time.

existing_optimizations_and_negative_find: Full scan supplies Some(shared WalkManifest): indexer.rs479–480 and build_plan passes it. Config signature and token discovery iterate/filter/sort that manifest separately but do not repeat the filesystem walk or stat; only matching config files are reread for tokens. If raw_tokens is empty, full-snapshot payload skips full symbol/file catalog clone and lookup construction (snapshot.rs77–85).

FTS schema reference is OnceLock cached. can_defer_snapshot_fts is checked once before file loop, not per file. Files/literal mirrors use256-file windows and new rowid ranges; no IN scan of growing prior-file prefixes in that path.

Snapshot eligible leaf tables/dependencies already use at most64rows/64KiB bounded windows with original64/8/1 binders; fields with fewer8rows keep row inserts. Chunk base+chunk FTS remain per chunk, and file_path/symbol FTS triggers still execute. No new recommendation to reimplement existing batching.
Prepared-statement cache capacity64 and prepare_cached calls already exist; no evidence that repeated compilation/cache eviction is the observed cost.
Fresh DB/schema creation and stale staging-file cleanup occur once per full, not once per source file. No repeated project-directory recreation or unconditional per-file whole-table scan identified.
conclusion: The broad staging clock legitimately includes most database materialization. Only one concrete repeated-work candidate is singled out; no source-only basis to declare a new necessary repair, quantify benefit, alter current study or add an acceptance gate. Original A/B timing remains source-bound and unchanged.
